name: vehicle-reposition-before-blast
description: Issue #1092 phase 6: the Fleet panel's new Reposition control drives a vehicle somewhere with no work attached (Itinerary's `reposition` Goal), the player-facing replacement for console-only `vehicle move`. Reuses blast-unevacuated-casualties.json's exact seed-42 drill/charge/sequence/fire pattern at (15,15)-(21,21) -- that file, with every staffed vehicle left exactly where it spawned, reports `vehicleCount` decreasing (the drill_rig it drove out on, plus a second vehicle the reckless 8m-hole/0.5m-stemming overcharge's flyrock reaches from spawn). This file moves the staffed debris_hauler (#2, spawned at (3,2) by STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION) well clear of both the drilled footprint and that flyrock radius BEFORE the same pattern fires, entirely by clicking: open the Fleet panel, click vehicle #2's Reposition button, pick a far tile, confirm. No console command anywhere in that step. The final `vehicle list`/`state full` observe steps are this scenario's actual proof for the visual channel -- state-schema-definitions.ts has no per-vehicle position/survival field for `expect` to check programmatically (same gap vehicle-driver-assignment-visual.json's own observe steps document), so a human (or an automated screenshot/state-dump read) confirms vehicle #2 is listed, parked at the safe tile, undamaged, after the blast that damages/destroys vehicles left in place.

steps.description: Vehicle #2 is the staffed debris_hauler (STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION order: drill_rig, debris_hauler, rock_digger, rock_fragmenter), spawned at (3,2) -- close to the drill_rig's own spawn and well inside range of the reckless overcharge fired later in this file. (2,30) is far south of both the (15,15)-(21,21) drilled footprint and the (0,2)-(9,2) spawn row. No `vehicle` console command reaches the game here -- Reposition arms the shared placement tool (PlacementKit, same pattern as SurveyPanel's Run Survey button), a scene-tile click picks the destination, and the confirm button dispatches the command internally.

Sandbox-measured pad: the auto-selected licensed driver (one of the two staffed driving.excavator drivers is NOT eligible -- debris_hauler needs driving.truck -- so the staffed driving.truck driver boards) walks to the debris_hauler and drives it clear well within 20 ticks. No pollable field exposes a specific vehicle's own position (same gap noted throughout this file), so this is a fixed pad rather than a wait_until, matching vehicle-driver-assignment-visual.json's own tick-30 pad for the same reason.

Mid-course observe: vehicle #2 should now read parked at (2,30), driver released (Mount.alight, once the reposition itinerary's drive leg completes with no further work queued). Proof for the visual channel -- no summary field carries a specific vehicle's own x/z.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:3 cols:3 spacing:3 depth:8 diameter:0.089 start:15,15
steps.description: Identical pattern to blast-unevacuated-casualties.json: 3x3 grid at the grid tool's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), so the (15,15)-(21,21) drag needs no spacing-stepper click. diameter:0.089 matches the Charge panel's fixed UI diameter (no stepper exists for it); the depth stepper is raised from the tool's 6m default to the declared 8m before dragging, same as that file's own fix.
Drains the ordered drill plan -- the staffed driller/drill_rig pair claims and drives the work entirely on its own, same as blast-unevacuated-casualties.json.

The same reckless, under-stemmed overcharge (0.5m on 8m holes) blast-unevacuated-casualties.json fires -- the whole point is that THIS exact pattern is dangerous enough to cost a vehicle when nothing is moved out of the way.
Blast panel is already open and BlastWorkshop's own autoAdvance has already moved it to the Sequence tab, same as blast-unevacuated-casualties.json -- ensurePanel avoids a toggle-closed click.

Fires the same deterministic pattern blast-unevacuated-casualties.json fires with nothing moved -- that file's `vehicleCount` decreases (the drill_rig it drove out on, plus a second vehicle the flyrock reaches). Vehicle #2, moved to (2,30) three steps ago, is far outside both the drilled footprint and that flyrock radius. This step's own `expect` only pins what's certain regardless of any single vehicle's fate (nothing here asserts total fleet survival); the follow-up observe steps are the actual proof that #2 specifically made it through.

Proof point: vehicle #2 must still be listed, parked at (2,30), undamaged -- state-schema-definitions.ts has no per-vehicle field for `expect` to check this programmatically, so this command's output (and the accompanying screenshot in interaction mode) is what the visual channel inspects.
